engagement_title: Apexguard Surface Systems dealer rollout: recover the drafted master mark as real artwork, bring a two-session install bay to one look, rebuild the printer's roll label into a live merge, and hand the dealer channel one editable set
vertical: Automotive, Industrial and Agriculture: paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating supplied to dealer groups and to independent installers who buy film by the roll (Charlotte, North Carolina)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork rebrand brief from a client who 'supplies paint protection film (PPF), window tint, and related products' and is 'rebranding and need a designer to deliver a complete logo and identity system that works on digital channels and physical packaging (boxes, labels, stickers)', with the visual direction stated as 'Premium, modern, performance-automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory-catalog, not tuner.', a required 'strong master + sub-brand naming' structure, and an explicit exclusion of 'mascots, vintage badges, heavy gradients.' Co-anchor: the Upwork logo-vectorization and brand-identity-kit brief from a client whose logo existed only as a low-resolution raster and who needed print-ready vector artwork plus print and apparel variations and a colour and type reference. Laundered to the fictional Apexguard Surface Systems; no real company, person, product or trademark appears, the mark is original geometry recovered from the client's own supplied artwork, and no craft-software brand name appears in any task-facing field. The ledger records this slot as previously sitting almost entirely on one authoring surface. LAYOUT-17 restores the commission both clients actually posted: the identity has to be recovered as usable artwork, and the point of recovering it is that a dealer deck, a counter poster, an installer social set and a printed roll label all carry it and all have to agree.
client_one_liner: A master mark we only have as a picture, three tiers that have to read as one family, a bay we shot on two different days, and a printer's roll label we cannot open, all due before the dealer meetings.
client_brief:
Apexguard Surface Systems, dealer rollout.

We supply paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating. We sell two ways: through dealer groups who resell our installs, and direct to independent installers who buy film by the roll. We are rebranding and we want the whole rollout in one designer's hands.

We had a master mark drafted for us. What we actually hold is a picture of it and the shop card we had printed from that draft. We need it back as real artwork we can put anywhere, from the top of a dealer deck down to the end of a film box, and we need the three tier marks alongside it so the family reads as one family rather than three logos.

Our own photography is the next problem. We shoot in our own bay. Some of it happened on a Saturday and the rest later in the week, and it does not hang together. Clear film has to still look clear and tinted glass has to still look like tint, because that is what the customer is buying.

Then the pieces. A deck we take into dealer groups. A spec poster for the counter at the installer shops. A set for the installers' own feeds, at the three shapes they post at. A tier comparison our sales people can point at, because the question in every meeting is what the difference between the three tiers actually is. A page that shows the mark family and how to use it. And the roll labels: our printer built those last year off our system, one label per roll, we have their file and nothing else, and this year's widths and warranty wording have to go through it without the label changing how it looks.

Premium, modern, performance automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory catalog, not tuner. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients. A full install runs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars on a car worth sixty thousand, so it has to look like that.

Send it all back as one file we can edit ourselves, and if anything in our data looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Full vehicle paint protection film installs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars; tint packages 400 to 1,200 dollars; film sold by the roll to installers at 900 to 4,200 dollars a roll. Two audiences: dealer group principals and fixed operations managers, 35 to 55, deciding whether to put Apexguard on their reconditioning line, and independent installer owners, 28 to 50, who buy film by the roll and post their own work. The vehicle owner behind both is 30 to 55 and protecting a 60,000 dollar car. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is precise and near technical: confident spacing, one restrained accent against a deep neutral, film performance stated as a plain table rather than as a burst, photography that is clean and even rather than dramatic. Push it toward discount tint shop grammar, starbursts, chrome bevels, percentage flashes, three exclamation colours, and a dealer principal reads it as a two hundred dollar tint job and stops believing the ten year warranty printed beside it, which is the exact failure the client describes when they say not factory catalog and not tuner. Push it the other way into moody cinematic car culture and it reads as an enthusiast page rather than a supplier a dealer group can put on its reconditioning line. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,200 to 4,500 dollars fixed, or 50 to 85 dollars an hour across 40 to 60 hours.

brand_identity.sector: Paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating supplied to dealer groups and to independent installers who buy film by the roll.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Charlotte, North Carolina, a small supplier running one install bay and a two person channel team.
brand_identity.about: Apexguard supplies paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating two ways: through dealer groups who resell our installs on their reconditioning line, and direct to independent installers who buy film by the roll. We sell performance that is stated plainly and warranted in writing, not a look. The brand is built around a master mark and three tier marks (Guard, Guard Pro, Guard Elite) that have to read as one family so a dealer sees one supplier, not three products.
brand_identity.audience: Dealer group principals and fixed operations managers aged 35 to 55 deciding whether to put us on their reconditioning line, and independent installer owners aged 28 to 50 who buy film by the roll and post their own work. Behind both sits a vehicle owner aged 30 to 55 protecting a sixty thousand dollar car.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Full PPF installs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars, tint packages 400 to 1,200 dollars, film by the roll to installers 900 to 4,200 dollars. Premium performance tier, well above discount tint shops and deliberately not tuner.
brand_identity.typography: A single near technical system: a tight modern grotesque for the mark, headings and tier names set in confident spacing, paired with a clean humanist sans for spec tables and body so performance numbers read as data. No display flourish, no italic drama.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, exact, performance led. States numbers and lets them carry. Example line the brand would write: Ten year warranty, self healing topcoat, 92 percent clarity retained. No exclamation points, no percentage flashes, no hype.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The rebrand mark was drafted for us by an earlier round and no working file survives. What we hold is a flat raster export of the drafted master mark and a phone photograph of the installer shop card that was printed from an earlier revision of it. The mark has to be recovered as real artwork before the rollout can carry it, and the three tier marks brought alongside so the family reads as one.
brand_identity.values: Performance stated honestly and warranted as written. One brand across every surface, from the top of a dealer deck to the end of a film box.

assets_supplied.name: master_mark_draft/ (mark_draft_2400.png plus shopcard_photo.jpg)
assets_supplied.kind: The drafted master mark supplied only as a flat 2400 px raster on a light ground, plus a phone photograph of the installer shop card that was printed from an earlier round of the same draft.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'The mark as it was drafted for us, and the card we had printed off it. That is everything we have. No working file.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The draft carries a hairline keyline around the shield and a narrow counter inside the inner chevron that survive a trace at canvas size and stop being holes at the sizes this mark actually gets used at, and nothing in the traced artwork declares that. The photographed shop card is an earlier revision whose chevron angle and wordmark tracking do not match the 2400 px file, so recovering the mark from whichever source is easier to select produces artwork that will not sit with the rest of the rollout.

assets_supplied.name: bay_frames/ (10 frames, 4600 x 3070)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house photography shot in the company's own install bay: film rolls on the rack, a car mid wrap, hood edge and door shut line close ups, tinted glass, a squeegee pull.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Our own bay, our own camera. Some of it on the Saturday, the rest later that week. It does not hang together.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bay runs sodium overheads at one end and LED work lamps at the other, and the two sessions were shot under different mixes, so half the range carries a green cast that reads as a film tint difference rather than as a lighting difference. Separately, the matte black film rolls sit on a dark grey steel rack at almost the same value, so an isolation of a roll reports success and quietly takes a bite out of the roll's own edge where the two meet.

assets_supplied.name: rolllabel_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The print shop's flat press PDF of last season's film roll box end label, 4 by 6 inches, one SKU per label, fonts embedded, produced from the company's own system through a full print engine. Carries the tier name, a width and length line, a six row performance block, a warranty statement and a small mark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'What the printer sent us last year. Nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it looking exactly like this and put this year's widths and wording through it.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at Apexguard could tell you. The label was set as one continuous flowing block, so the tier name, the width line, the performance rows and the warranty statement all convert into a single story with no per field frames to map, and everything has to be driven by ordered offsets inside that one story. And the warranty block sits in a fixed measure frame sized to last season's shorter wording: a longer statement does not spill and does not flag, it simply stops rendering where the frame ends, and every response in the chain still reports success.

assets_supplied.name: skus_and_tiers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the company's stock system, one row per film roll SKU, with columns for SKU code, tier, width, roll length, the six performance parameters, warranty statement, dealer price and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Straight out of our system. The performance numbers and the warranty wording are ours and we are held to them as written.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Fourteen rows for twelve live SKUs: two superseded widths the system still emits, marked only by a withdrawn date column the client never mentions. Tier names carry trailing spaces from the spreadsheet that exported them, the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, and three warranty statements rewritten by the legal reviewer run roughly four times the length of the others.

assets_supplied.name: brand_direction.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page of written direction from the owner, in plain language, with no colour values and no type names.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Premium, modern, performance automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory catalog, not tuner. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.'

acceptance_bar: The master mark comes back as artwork that scales, sits clean and transparent on any ground including our deep neutral, and holds together at the smallest place we actually use it. If there is a size below which it must not be used, say so and give us the version that covers it.
The three tier marks read as one family with the master. A dealer looking at all four should see one brand, not three logos.
Only one revision of the mark exists in the delivered work. Every piece carries the same artwork.
All ten bay frames read as one bay on one day, judged with them laid out together rather than one at a time. Clear film still reads as clear and tinted glass still reads as tint.
Isolated film rolls are cut on their own edge, with nothing bitten out of the roll and nothing of the rack left attached.
No delivered file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

Roll labels: exactly one label per live SKU, every field the 2025 label carried present on every label, every value bound verbatim from our export, and the mark on each label the delivered artwork rather than last year's.
Nothing in our export may be shortened, reworded or abbreviated to make it fit. Anything that will not fit inside the label as it stands, tell us in writing before it goes to the printer.
The press file renders at real print resolution at label trim, and there is one label file per SKU named to the SKU code, containing the SKU its name claims.

The dealer deck, the counter poster, the installer social set, the tier comparison and the mark family page come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from.
In that file the words are live text, the tier comparison is a real table and the marks are real artwork we can recolour, not pictures of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
Nothing flashy: no mascot, no vintage badge, no heavy gradient, no burst.

A written note: what was done to each picture and why it differs from its neighbours, which mark source you used and why, anything in our export you questioned and what you did about it, and anything the label could not carry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging (includes image_vectorize, which is a Photoshop family tool and is not counted as an Illustrator surface)
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_single_color_saturation, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.detection_confidence and metadata.tradeoffs, image_remove_background with and without backgroundColor, image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Recovers the master mark from a flat raster as scalable vector artwork, including the viewBox injection and the removal of the opaque full canvas path that the trace always emits. Produces the three tier colourways from the one recovered plate using the same mask with different parameters, so the family is genuinely one piece of artwork rather than three drawings. Brings ten frames shot under two different lighting mixes to one neutral with a per frame parameter set, protects clear film and tinted glass from being flattened into each other, and cuts the roll and hood edge isolations where subject and ground sit at nearly the same value.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and as validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the printer's flat roll label into a live merge template with no working file to start from, reads the real frame inventory and the true story text before promising any field map, binds the recovered mark and the per SKU values into a label that must keep its printed appearance, and runs the live SKUs at one record per label to a press file plus per SKU named labels plus 300 ppi proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: Everything the client does not have: a six root dealer deck, an A1 counter poster at true physical dimensions, an installer social set at three canvas shapes in the same document, the tier comparison as a genuine table, and the mark family basis page carrying the recovered artwork as live vector. One export, roots at their own declared canvas sizes, every photograph carried as embedded image data because a photograph referenced by URL arrives as an empty box.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles for the numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts for name laundering, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the deck, the poster, the social set and the basis page, and its specification in the handover. The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair, and it has to land premium and near technical rather than aftermarket. The handover also has to state that no face from this surface can reach the printed roll label, because there is no font file to install on that surface, so the label's typography stays the printer's.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted together as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed vehicle or road context frame for the deck opener and the counter poster, which the company cannot shoot because it never has a finished customer car outside the bay, plus the persistent board the owner and the two dealer account managers approve the rollout from before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The labels are one record per label against a layout the client has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The deck, poster, social set, tier table and basis page do not exist yet, need several canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Trying to merge the poster discovers that one record per page cannot produce three canvas shapes; authoring the label from scratch throws away the look the printer already produced.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload both mark sources, the ten bay frames, the 2025 label PDF and the stock system export, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline. Thirty artefacts later the mapping between URL, SKU and role has to still be trustworthy, and two of the artefacts are two revisions of the same mark.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by asset and role.

trajectory.action: Preview both mark sources and all ten bay frames and triage: which mark revision is current, which session each frame came from, how level it is, and where subject and background sit at the same value.
trajectory.judgement: Two pictures of what the client calls the same mark are not the same mark, and choosing between them is a decision about what the whole rollout will carry. The frames also have to be read for value collision before anything is derived from them, since the client describes only a lighting problem.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering mark revision, session, level and subject to ground separation.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes every crop decision rather than following one.

trajectory.action: Fix one neutral from the better lit session and correct each frame toward it with its own parameter set, recording what was dialled per frame.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across ten frames rather than ten locally pleasing pictures. The frames shot under the other lamp mix need a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral, and a single batched call would apply one identical set and ship half the bay green.
trajectory.produces: Ten graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections so clear film still reads as clear and tinted glass still reads as tint rather than as a grey wash, and the black rolls keep their material without going flat.
trajectory.judgement: This is the client's commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one, because clarity and tint level are what is being sold. Prompt wording is the whole gate, and a material selection on a dark roll lying on a dark rack can leak into the rack, which has to be read as leakage rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Frames whose film and glass behaviour survives the grade, with the masked parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the master mark from the chosen source: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties rather than the sheet it sits on, invert, crop to the mask's own bounds, trace to SVG, then inject a viewBox and strip the opaque full canvas path the trace always emits.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle. The trace ships with no viewBox and an opaque background rectangle, and neither is announced, so an untouched trace is a white box on the deck's deep neutral.
trajectory.produces: A scalable transparent master mark as SVG artwork.

trajectory.action: Produce the three tier colourways from the one recovered plate using the same mask with different parameters, and record the parameters dialled per tier.
trajectory.judgement: The family has to be one piece of artwork carrying three treatments, because that is what makes the tiers read as a family. Hue movement here is an adjacent move, not a jump to a named colour, so the tier separation has to be designed within what the range actually reaches.
trajectory.produces: Three tier colourways of the master mark plus the per tier parameter record.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging and Adobe Express
trajectory.action: Place the master mark and the smallest tier lockup at their true reproduction sizes on the real grounds they will sit on, the deck's deep neutral and the roll label's box end, and look at them there.
trajectory.judgement: Artwork is judged where it is used, at the size it is used, on the ground it is used on. A mark inspected at canvas size on white has not been inspected.
trajectory.produces: Placement proofs of the mark and the smallest lockup at true size on the real grounds.

trajectory.action: Cut the film roll and hood edge isolations onto the studio ground for the poster and the social set, routing per frame, and check each cut edge against its source.
trajectory.judgement: A one call knockout is right for a roll standing clear of the rack and wrong where roll and rack share value, and the wrong route returns a plausible cutout with the roll's own edge bitten away. The route is a per frame decision made by looking at the frame.
trajectory.produces: Isolations on the studio ground with the route recorded per frame.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the stock export against the roll rack photography and the tier direction, normalise it into a merge shaped file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the label artwork and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real data preparation work: superseded rows the system still emits, tier names carrying spreadsheet whitespace, and an image column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which are the client's, and how to say so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded label artwork, the image map, and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2025 label to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the client's own system happened to produce rather than by the plan, and the readout a tool hands you is not automatically the same string as the document's own.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every label field plus the mark, ordering any rows that share a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that actually came back, computing offsets from a source of truth chosen deliberately, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the label fields and the mark frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before any label exists.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the mark bound, render the press file and 300 ppi proofs at label trim, produce per SKU labels named to the SKU code, and read every rendered label against its export row at true trim rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to a press file forfeits the per record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming twelve labels by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one an installer discovers on a rack.
trajectory.produces: The press label file, 300 ppi proofs, per SKU identity verified labels, and a line by line reconciliation at true trim.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one vehicle or road context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house neutral and judge it beside the bay frames.
trajectory.judgement: A context frame at this band has to be restrained and plausible rather than dramatic. A night lit hero car is the wrong register for a supplier a dealer group is being asked to put on its reconditioning line.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read premium and near technical rather than aftermarket. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML holding the six dealer deck roots, the A1 counter poster at true physical dimensions, the three installer social canvases, the tier comparison as a real table and the mark family basis page carrying the recovered artwork as inline vector, each root declaring its own canvas size, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and every other canvas through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview shows only the first canvas, so the export is unverified until the markup is read canvas by canvas. The design decisions, how much of the A1 is table and how much is photograph, whether the deck opens on the mark or on the warranty, are the actual work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document holding every canvas, its durable source HTML, and a per canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the recovered mark family, the graded bay and the licensed frame, within the placement cap and re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to let the next freelancer rebuild the label from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name the warranty wording that will not fit and the export rows that were excluded, before a printer sees the file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the sizes it is actually used at, on the grounds it is actually used on. The trace is clean and correct at canvas size on white: the shield keyline is a hairline, the inner chevron counter is a hole, the tier lockup's small type is separated. Placed at its true reproduction size on the deck's deep neutral and at box end size on the roll label, the counter closes into a solid, the keyline either disappears or merges with the shield edge, and the tier word thickens into a bar. Nothing in the trace, the artwork or any response reports this, because at the moment of tracing the artwork is genuinely correct. It becomes wrong only in the relationship between this particular drafted geometry, this particular reproduction size and this particular ground, none of which exist as a number anywhere.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either: a trace that is faithful to the draft is the correct output of the tracing step, and the tool takes no options that would change the result, so there is no first time to get right. Nothing states it, because the brief asks for artwork that holds at the smallest place it is used, which is an ordinary client requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description mentions the keyline or the counter. And the response is not a re-run: the mark has to be re-derived from a differently prepared raster, a minimum size rule has to be written that did not previously exist, and a small size variant has to be designed and then adopted across the label, the social set and the basis page.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mark from a mask prepared differently at the raster stage, since the trace itself has no lever, and judge the result again at true size on the deep neutral rather than at canvas size. Where the geometry still will not hold at label size, author a simplified small size variant, write the minimum size rule and the variant into the mark family basis page, and go back through the label mapping and the social set so both carry the variant they should be carrying rather than the master.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rollout in which the mark is a legible piece of artwork in the deck and a dark blob on every film roll box in every installer shop, delivered to a client whose entire brief was an identity that works on digital channels and on physical packaging.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's label actually exposes, and then whether the merged labels carry what the export says. The label was set as one continuous flowing block, so tier name, width line, performance rows and warranty statement all convert into a single story with no per field frames, and the mapping has to be driven entirely by ordered offsets. The second fact only arrives at trim: the warranty block sits in a fixed measure frame sized to last season's shorter wording, so the three longer statements do not spill, do not reflow and do not raise an overset flag anywhere. The text simply stops at the frame edge, mid sentence, on those three labels, and the merge response, the render response and the label at proof scale all look correct.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The truncation is worse: a fixed frame that stops rendering produces no error, no warning and no visual alarm at proof scale, so an agent that maps carefully, validates cleanly and renders successfully still ships three wrong labels. It is not a propagation re-run either, because the answer is not to re-merge: it is to decide, with the client, what happens to wording that cannot be shortened inside a frame that cannot be resized.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered label at true trim rather than at proof scale, against its export row, word by word through the warranty statement. Confirm the frame measure from the document rather than from the rendered page, establish which statements exceed it, and escalate in writing before the press file is committed, since the acceptance bar forbids shortening or rewording anything to make it fit. Re-plan the mark binding at the same time if the placement proof from the earlier checkpoint changed which variant the label should carry.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve film roll labels printed and shipped in which three carry a warranty statement that stops mid sentence, sold to installers who resell that warranty to a vehicle owner, with every tool in the chain having reported success and the proof having looked right.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did with the three constructs the rollout depends on: the tier comparison carried in as a real table with per cell strokes, the recovered mark family carried in as inline vector, and the installer social canvases carried in at shapes different from the deck. None of those can be confirmed by any channel other than reading the markup the import returns, and every drop this importer performs comes back as an unqualified success. The multi canvas shape compounds it, because the visual preview resolves only the first canvas, so whatever happened on the poster, the social set and the basis page is reported by the returned markup and by nothing else.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: How this importer normalises a given construct is not documented anywhere the agent can read ahead, is not a parameter, and is not signalled by the response status, so authoring more carefully does not tell you what happened. Nothing states it: the brief asks for live text, a real table and artwork that can be recoloured, which is the client's requirement for a file they can edit, and names no importer and no failure. And the response is not a re-run, because a construct that did not survive has to be re-authored in a different form, and the layout around it changes with it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup per canvas, not only the first, and check that every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the mark arrived as path shapes rather than one flattened element, that the comparison arrived as real cells rather than a stack of loose text, that every text element carries the intended face and the intended numeric weight rather than a silent fallback, and that no element resolves past its declared canvas width. Re-author whichever constructs did not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and inspect again rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dealer deck and counter poster handed over as the client's editable file in which the tier comparison is a heap of loose text and the mark family page is empty geometry, discovered by a sales manager in front of a dealer group because the only canvas anyone looked at was the first one.

decision_gates: The surface split: labels to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one record per label, everything else to HTML authoring because it needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which of two supplied mark sources is the current revision, knowing the whole rollout carries whichever one is chosen.
How the mark is named in the selection prompt, since naming the sheet it sits on pulls the mask to the sheet and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle.
Whether the recovered mark holds at true reproduction size on the deep neutral and at label size, and what the minimum size rule should therefore be.
How far to separate the three tier colourways within the hue movement actually available, so the tiers read as a family rather than as three brands.
Which session sets the neutral, and how far to correct the other before the correction itself becomes a visible film tint change.
Isolation route per frame, where a one call knockout is right for a roll standing clear of the rack and returns a bitten edge where roll and rack share value.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's own label story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
How to honour nothing shortened or reworded when three warranty statements exceed a frame that cannot be resized.
Whether to name twelve labels by the order they came back or by opening each one.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a premium performance automotive readership, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed label at all.
Whether the licensed context frame reads as a supplier a dealer group would adopt or as enthusiast car photography.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and it returns handsome pictures of cars and a new logo. IDENTITY: the client already has a drafted master mark and needs that specific geometry recovered and carried, from the top of a deck down to a box end, with three tier treatments that are demonstrably the same artwork. A regenerated mark is a different logo, and a rollout whose deck logo and label logo are different logos is the exact failure the client is paying to avoid. SPEC: the client needs one label per live SKU at 4 by 6 inch trim and 300 ppi, twelve separately named label files each containing the SKU their filename claims, six performance values and a warranty statement bound verbatim from their own stock export with nothing reworded, an A1 poster at true physical dimensions, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season's widths are a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and recolourable vector artwork so tier pricing can move. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, does this counter still exist at label size, did this cut follow the roll's edge or the rack's, is this warranty statement complete at trim. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). Five surfaces, honestly counted: image_vectorize is declared as a Photoshop family tool and no Illustrator surface is claimed, since document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host. MARK RECOVERY: select_by_prompt at ink level, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds driven by returnBbox, and vectorize are verified end to end on a printed mark photographed on a surface, including the documented substrate versus material prompt asymmetry, the missing viewBox and the path zero opaque rectangle that must be stripped by hand. The reproduction size checkpoint rests on documented facts rather than assumption: vectorize takes no options at all, so raster preparation is the only lever, and the trace's fidelity to fine geometry is exactly what makes it fail small. TIER COLOURWAYS: image_apply_adjustments with a shared maskURI and differing hsl parameters is verified as a masked colour variant system, with the documented caveat that range holds at moderate, so the tiers are designed as adjacent moves rather than jumps to named hexes. ISOLATIONS: remove_background with and without backgroundColor is verified, along with its silent downscale tradeoff and its failure on subjects that do not separate cleanly, and the select then invert then fill route is verified as the alternative. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the press file branch, per record named files are confirmed by two order verified routes while multi record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. The label PDF is specified as a real font embedding press PDF from a full engine, since a thin hand authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. THE COLLAPSED STORY IS A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 observed that a continuous text flow converts to exactly one text frame, which is precisely what this label is built to produce, and the fixed measure truncation is a frame geometry consequence rather than a claimed tool behaviour. IMAGE BINDING: per row binding through an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified, and the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback that also guarantees per record identity. EXPRESS: multi root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 is a true physical canvas, tables survive as real tables with per cell strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, transport is routed through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview resolves page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end and the task leans on the non standard numeric weights, the slug not PostScript rule and the all or nothing kit call; the impossibility of putting a font on the InDesign surface is stated as a client facing constraint rather than silently ignored. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, never the broken orientation filter, licensing returns genuine camera scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
